evals.name: li-seed-round
evals.prompt: I just closed our seed round — $3.2M led by Hustle Fund after 47 investor meetings and something like 41 nos. Took 7 months. Biggest lesson honestly was that we pitched the product way too much and the market not enough; once we flipped the deck to lead with the market shift (small clinics getting pushed into value-based care contracts) it took 3 weeks to fill the round. Write me a LinkedIn post about it. I'm the cofounder of Carelane, we do care coordination software for small clinics.
evals.expected_output: A plain-text LinkedIn post (no markdown) with a short, specific hook inside ~140 characters, built on the user's real numbers (47 meetings, 41 nos, 7 months, 3 weeks, $3.2M), one clear lesson (pitch the market shift, not the product), no invented details, no engagement bait or AI tells, plus two alternative hooks and brief notes.
assertions: The post contains no markdown bold or headings
The first line is under ~140 characters
Uses at least three of the user's real specifics
Does not invent investor names, quotes or metrics the user didn't give
No 'It's not X, it's Y' reframe and none of the stock phrases the skill lists
No engagement bait (comment YES, 'Agree?', like if)
0-3 hashtags and at most 1 emoji
Provides two alternative hooks

evals.name: li-fix-draft
evals.prompt:
can you fix my linkedin post before I post it tomorrow morning. be honest

---
🚀 In today's fast-paced world of product management, I've learned that it's not about building features, it's about solving problems.

Last quarter our team shipped 23 features. Our NPS went down.

Here's the thing: customers don't care about your roadmap. They care about outcomes.

So we made a change. We cut our roadmap in half and spent 6 weeks doing nothing but customer interviews (62 of them!).

The result? Retention up 14%. Support tickets down 30%.

✅ Listen more
✅ Build less
✅ Measure what matters

Let that sink in. 💡

Agree? Comment "YES" if you've seen this too! 👇

#productmanagement #product #leadership #startups #customerexperience #growth
---
evals.expected_output: An honest diagnosis quoting the weak lines (cliché opener, 'it's not X it's Y', 'Here's the thing', 'The result?', emoji bullets, 'Let that sink in', engagement bait, six hashtags), then a rewrite that leads with the strong real material (23 features, NPS down, 62 interviews, +14% retention, -30% tickets) and keeps the user's facts.
assertions: The diagnosis flags the engagement bait ('Comment YES')
The diagnosis flags the AI-tell phrases
The rewrite keeps all the user's real numbers and adds no new ones
The rewrite's hook leads with a concrete specific (for example 23 features and NPS down)
The rewrite has no emoji bullets and at most 3 hashtags
The rewrite contains none of the flagged phrases

evals.name: li-topic-only
evals.prompt: write a linkedin post about why engineering managers should stop doing weekly status meetings. I'm an eng manager at a fintech, 12 people on my team. make it good
evals.expected_output: Either one short round of questions or a draft built on a structure that doesn't depend on invented personal claims (contrarian take, observation or how-to), using only the given facts (eng manager, fintech, team of 12). Any personal result, metric or anecdote is a marked [placeholder] or a question, not an invented story. Plain text, short hook, no bait, two alternative hooks and notes listing what to fill in.
assertions: Does not invent a story, metric or result about the user's team (for example hours saved, a quote from a team member, or a specific incident) and present it as true
Any missing personal detail is a clearly marked [placeholder] or a question in the notes, with no more than three placeholders in the post
Uses a structure that works without personal claims (contrarian take, observation, how-to or framework) or a story structure with placeholders
The hook is a claim, not a question, and fits in ~140 characters
Plain text with no markdown, at most 1 emoji and at most 3 hashtags
No engagement bait and no 'It's not X, it's Y' reframe
